1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The exam at a glance. The four domains and the eleven objective groups. What is new and where each layer fits. A four-step method for scenario questions. A study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All domains: exam format, domain map and answer technique. Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: The exam at a glance
1.text: The exam at a glance. The P L three hundred exam tests the Microsoft Power B I Data Analyst role: you prepare data, model it, build and analyze reports, and manage and secure content. It is an associate-level exam.

1.title: The exam at a glance, continued
1.text: The exam at a glance. The figure shows this: Map of the four P L three hundred domains with their weights and the course modules that teach each one.

1.title: The exam at a glance, continued
1.text: The exam at a glance. Time. one hundred minutes. Passing score. seven hundred on a scale of one thousand. Delivery. Proctored; items may include interactive components. Languages. ten; the English exam is updated first, the others about eight weeks later. Credential. Associate-level role-based credential. Renewal. Every twelve months with a free online assessment on Microsoft Learn. Retake. After twenty-four hours; later retakes wait longer. Content. Mostly generally available features; preview features appear if commonly used.

1.title: The exam at a glance, continued
1.text: The exam at a glance. Use the current Practice Assessment on A I Skills Navigator. The older practice assessments on Microsoft Learn are no longer updated. Read the study guide page again before you book, because the skills list can change. Exam tip: one hundred minutes, a passing score of seven hundred on a scale of one thousand, a retake after twenty-four hours, and renewal every twelve months with a free online assessment. Renewal is an assessment, not a second exam.

1.title: The four domains and the 11 objective groups
1.text: The four domains and the eleven objective groups. The study guide lists seventy-eight skills. They sit in eleven objective groups inside four domains. This course teaches them in modules one to fifteen. Module zero is this orientation and module sixteen is the final review.

1.title: The four domains and the 11 objective groups, continued
1.text: The four domains and the eleven objective groups. Prepare the data, twenty-five-thirty percent. Objective groups: Get or connect to data; Profile and clean the data; Transform and load the data. Modules: one to four. Model the data, twenty-five-thirty percent. Objective groups: Design and implement a data model; Create model calculations by using dacks; Optimize model performance. Modules: five to eight. Visualize and analyze the data, twenty-five-thirty percent. Objective groups: Create reports; Enhance reports for usability and storytelling; Identify patterns and trends. Modules: nine to thirteen.

1.title: The four domains and the 11 objective groups, continued
1.text: The four domains and the eleven objective groups. Manage and secure Power B I, fifteen-twenty percent. Objective groups: Create and manage workspaces and assets; Secure and govern Power B I items. Modules: fourteen and fifteen.

1.title: The four domains and the 11 objective groups, continued
1.text: The four domains and the eleven objective groups. The three large domains carry the same weight. Manage and secure Power B I is the smallest, but its facts are precise and testable: roles, refresh limits, row-level security and labels. Exam tip: Three domains weigh twenty-five-thirty percent each and Manage and secure Power B I weighs fifteen-twenty percent. Do not skip the smallest domain: its limits and role rules are easy to learn and easy to test.

1.title: What is new and where each layer fits
1.text: What is new and where each layer fits. The skills list names several newer topics. Give them extra time if you studied with older material. Choosing between Direct Lake, Direct Query and Import. one. Calculation groups. seven. dacks query view, with Performance Analyzer. eight. Visual calculations and Copilot (narrative visual, create a report page, suggest content). ten. Personalization and accessibility. twelve. Copilot to summarize the semantic model. thirteen. In the latest update only three groups changed, and only slightly: Get or connect to data, Enhance reports for usability and storytelling, and Create and manage workspaces and assets. Every question belongs to one layer. Naming the layer removes most wrong answers.

1.title: What is new and where each layer fits, continued
1.text: What is new and where each layer fits. Power Query Editor. Job: Shape data before it loads. Examples: Data types, errors, merge, append, pivot, parameters. Model. Job: Define tables and relationships. Examples: Relationships, cardinality, date table, row-level security roles. dacks. Job: Calculate inside the model. Examples: Measures, calculated columns, calculation groups. Report. Job: Show and explore. Examples: Visuals, themes, slicers, bookmarks, drillthrough. Service. Job: Share, refresh and secure. Examples: Workspaces, apps, scheduled refresh, gateway, labels. Exam tip: Find the layer first. Data types and null values are Power Query, filter context is dacks, a drillthrough page is the report, and scheduled refresh is the service.

1.title: A four-step method for scenario questions
1.text: A four-step method for scenario questions. Most items describe a short business situation and ask for the best feature or the first action. Use the same four steps every time. Find the layer. Is the problem in Power Query, the model, dacks, the report or the service? Find the requirement words. Words such as "without", "only", "must", "least effort" and "live" decide the answer. Remove options that break a requirement. An option that needs code breaks "without writing code". Choose the simplest built-in feature. If two options work, take the one that is built in and needs the least effort.

1.title: A four-step method for scenario questions, continued
1.text: A four-step method for scenario questions. Without writing code. A built-in feature, such as a quick measure or a conditional column. Before the data loads. The Power Query Editor. Data must not be copied, or live. Direct Query, Direct Lake or a shared semantic model. Only some users see some rows. Row-level security, which applies to Viewers. Each viewer changes the visual. Personalization. Pixel-perfect or printing. A paginated report. Exam tip: When two options work, the exam prefers the built-in feature over code, a custom visual or an extra tool. Check each option against every requirement word.

2.title: A study plan
2.text: A study plan. Learn each feature by doing it in Power B I Desktop, which is free. Items may include interactive components, so know where each command lives, not only its name. one. Modules: one to four. Practice: Clean and reshape a messy file in the Power Query Editor. two. Modules: five to eight. Practice: Build a star schema, a date table and measures. three. Modules: nine to thirteen. Practice: Build a report with slicers, bookmarks and drillthrough. four. Modules: fourteen and fifteen. Practice: Use a workspace: roles, refresh, row-level security. five. Modules: sixteen. Practice: Chooser tables, look-alike terms and a practice assessment. After each module, answer its Q and A without the notes. Write one line for every look-alike pair, such as Import and Direct Query, then repeat the weak ones.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A candidate does not reach the passing score on a first attempt. What is the minimum wait before the retake? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: After twenty-four hours. A retake is allowed after twenty-four hours, and later retakes wait longer.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A data analyst holds the credential and wants to keep it valid. What does the renewal require? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A free online assessment on Microsoft Learn each year. The credential is renewed every twelve months with a free online assessment, not with a new exam.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A Date column holds a time part that stops it from matching the Date table. In which layer do you remove the time part before the data loads? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The Power Query Editor, by changing the type to Date. Data types are changed in the Power Query Editor, before the data loads into the model.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. You read a scenario about a viewer who must see only one region's sales rows. According to the four-step method, what should you do first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Decide which layer the question belongs to. The first step is to find the layer, because that removes the options from other layers.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A scenario says the report author cannot write code and needs a column that tags large orders. Which option follows the method? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Add a Conditional Column in Power Query. The built-in Conditional Column needs no code, so the other options break the requirement.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. How do the four domain weights compare? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Three weigh twenty-five-thirty percent and one weighs fifteen-twenty percent. Prepare, Model and Visualize weigh twenty-five-thirty percent each, and Manage and secure Power B I weighs fifteen-twenty percent.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How long is the exam? Answer: one hundred minutes. Question two. What score is required to pass? Answer: seven hundred on a scale of one thousand. Question three. Which domain has the lowest weight? Answer: Manage and secure Power B I, at fifteen-twenty percent.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the four steps for a scenario question? Answer: Find the layer, find the requirement words, remove options that break a requirement, choose the simplest built-in feature. Question five. In which layer do you merge and append queries? Answer: The Power Query Editor. Question six. Name the Copilot topics in the skills list. Answer: Narrative visual, create a report page, suggest content for a page, and summarize the semantic model.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Format: one hundred minutes; seven hundred on a scale of one thousand; proctored; may include interactive components. Credential: associate level; renewal every twelve months by a free online assessment. Domains: Prepare twenty-five-thirty percent; Model twenty-five-thirty percent; Visualize and analyze twenty-five-thirty percent; Manage and secure fifteen-twenty percent. Layers: Power Query Editor shapes, model relates, dacks calculates, report shows, service shares and secures. Newer topics: Direct Lake, calculation groups, dacks query view, visual calculations, Copilot, personalization, accessibility. Method: find the layer; find the requirement words; remove options that break a requirement. Study: practice each feature in Power B I Desktop; use the current Practice Assessment. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
